refnamediv.refpurpose: Compute the frequency response of a digital filter.

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: [h, w] = freqz(b, a) [h, w] = freqz(b, a, n) [h, w] = freqz(b, a, n, "whole") [h, w] = freqz(b, a, w) [h, f] = freqz(b, a, n, Fs) freqz(b, a, n) freqz(b, a)

listitem.para: Vector. The numerator coefficients of the filter's transfer function.
Vector. The denominator coefficients of the filter's transfer function. If omitted, it is assumed to be 1 (FIR filter).
Integer (optional). The number of frequency points. Default is 512.
Vector (optional). Specific frequencies (in radians) at which to evaluate the response.
Positive scalar (optional). Sampling frequency in Hz. If provided, frequencies are returned in Hz instead of radians.
Vector. The complex frequency response of the filter.
Vector. The frequencies (in radians) at which the response is evaluated.
Vector. The frequencies (in Hz) at which the response is evaluated.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: This function computes the frequency response of a digital filter defined by its numerator (`b`) and denominator (`a`) coefficients. The response can be evaluated at a specified number of points (`n`) or at specific frequencies (`w`). If the sampling frequency (`Fs`) is provided, the frequencies are returned in Hz.

- If `a` is omitted, the filter is assumed to be an FIR filter. - If `n` is omitted, a default value of 512 is used. - If the "whole" option is specified, the response is evaluated over the entire Nyquist range (0 to 2π). Otherwise, it is evaluated over half the Nyquist range (0 to π). - If no output arguments are provided, the function plots the magnitude and phase response.
